newsitem.title: UK: ACPC to decide future of coffee market mechanism.
newsitem.headline: ACPC to decide future of coffee market mechanism.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) will hold a full council meeting on May 21 to decide whether to introduce a new market mechanism after June.

The meeting, to be preceded by a technical group meeting on May 19, will also assess its current export programme, which was aimed at limiting member exports at 24.48 million bags in the first half if 1997.

The current programme which limit supplies through quota system expires at the end of June. The group members had been asked to consider if they plan to stick to the quota system or devise other mechanism.
In January, the 14-member group cut exports by 1.3 million bags to 24.98 million. But at a subsequent meeting in March, the group decided to put back some 500,000 bags on to the market.
ACPC officials were unable to say now if members had kept to their quotas.
"We are waiting for the meeting to get to know the situation in each member countries," ACPC secretary-general Roberio Oliveira Silva said on Wednesday.

There had been some concern a high level of shipments in the first quarter of this year together with export registrations for the April to June period would push top ACPC producer Brazil considerably over the its six million 60-kg bags January-to-June export limit.

As of April 25, the country's coffee export registrations totalled 3.20 million bags for April, May and June. Brazil in the first three months of 1997 sold 3.89 million bags according to Brazil's Coffee Exporters Federation (Febec) data.
But Brazilian government officials have said that the country was on course to meet its six million bag target.
"We should be around six million bags, perhaps a little more, perhaps a little less," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
Analysts said while the export intentions had been large, the actual loading and shipment had been rather slow.
But with the high current prices, the ACPC might be more flexible in dealing with quota-busting members.

In March, the ACPC allowed additional exports of 200,000 bags by Central American producer members who had sold heavily in the first quarter of this year amid a dazzling price rally seen earlier this year.

ACPC's Silva also said there had been several new market stabilisation proposals from members. These proposals would be studied by the technical group, comprising some key members, before a decision by the policy-making council.
Both the ACPC meetings coincide with the week-long International Coffee Organization meeting, also in London. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
